newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs sold early Monday at prices steady to mostly $0.50 per cwt lower than Friday's tops, with declines fueled by ongoing light demand by packers still dealing with unprofitable operating margins, livestock dealers said.

Declines were furthered by moderate hog marketings as weekend rain in the eastern Corn Belt saturated fields and kept farmers from late fieldwork, they said. The delay provided ample opportunities to sort and ship hogs instead.
Interior Iowa/so. Minnesota hogs sold steady-$0.50 lower at $53.00-$54.50 in the country and $54.50-$55.50 at plants.
Limited sales in the area were reported at $56.00.
Illinois hog prices sold steady, but with a weak tone and could turn lower as the day progressed, with $54.00 to $55.50 paid in the country and up to $56.00 plants, the dealers said.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower, at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $55.50 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $52.00 to $52.50 in the country $54.00 to $55.00 at plants, they said.
Weakness in the western Corn Belt also was tied to the temporary suspension of the second shift at the John Morrell plant in Sioux Falls, S.D. this week, sources there said.
